spec_match.rationale: Implements the explainer's Example 1 exactly — a horizontally-pannable table with sticky top and left labels inside an overflow: scroll clip wrapper — and explains the per-axis sticky containment rule the change introduces.

interactive.rationale: The table genuinely pans, the page scrolls, and live position measurements (label left-edge vs wrapper, header top vs viewport) update on both scroll sources.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the flagship layout with measured positions; delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: The page detects and honestly reports the legacy-conversion state (header trapped by the wrapper) rather than claiming the new behavior everywhere.

references.rationale: Feature index cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5067363861004288; page links the explainer's original jsbin.

conformance.rationale: The suite's sticky-constrained-per-axis manual assertion points at exactly this stage's interaction; automatable computed-value contracts run live.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CDP run: panned the table 120px and scrolled the page 300px — row label held at ~2px from the wrapper edge (sticky-left working), header measured moving with the wrapper (legacy behavior, honestly labelled); zero console errors; 0px page overflow both classes; screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: saxis-sticky-stage asserts with the computed overflowY driving the narrative.

design_system.rationale: Sticky header uses text-black bg + ivory text; row labels bg-stone + charcoal (AA); CSS variables only.

accessibility.rationale: Real table with scoped col/row headers; the pannable wrapper is a focusable labelled region; measurements are text in a bordered meter.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The wide table pans inside its own wrapper; page body 0px overflow at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×2000.

openQuestions.title: Measure the header tracking the viewport on Chrome 153
openQuestions.detail: On a true-clip engine the header-top-vs-viewport measurement should hold near 0 while the page scrolls past the wrapper. Capture that measurement to complete the before/after story.

guidanceConsulted.query: sticky table headers pannable wrapper page scroll
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Sticky both-axis labels belong on real table headers inside the scroll container that owns the relevant axis.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: thead th sticky top, tbody th sticky left, corner cell double-sticky with raised z-index.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Pannable regions need focusability and a name.

summary: Verified headlessly (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): panning and page scrolling drive real measurements on Chromium 141, with the legacy trap behavior detected and labelled instead of asserted away. The true-clip measurement on Chrome 153 is the open question.
